programme.title: Ibsen
programme.desc: 'To the May sun of a September life', wrote Henrik Ibsen on the photograph of himself that he gave to 19-year-old Emilie Bardach in Gossensass in September 1889. A look at the sixty-second year in the life of the great Norwegian dramatist.

programme.title: The Read
programme.sub-title: Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde: The Read with Reece Shearsmith
programme.desc: Who is the real monster? Robert Louis Stevenson's defining gothic horror explores alter egos in this captivating narration that reimagines the 19th-century classic.

programme.title: Munro: Mountain Man
programme.desc: Little more than 100 years ago, Scottish mountains standing at more than 3,000 feet were virtually unknown. Today they are familiar terrain to many thousands of climbers, thanks to Victorian adventurer Hugh Munro's determination to list the high peaks which now define the Highlands and Islands of Scotland. Nicholas Crane tells the story of the magnificent peaks that bear his name.

programme.title: Mysteries of the Bayeux Tapestry
programme.desc: The Bayeux Tapestry is a remarkable and unique work of art that has survived for almost 1,000 years. Made in the 11th century, it tells the story of William of Normandy's claim to the English throne, culminating in the Norman invasion of England and the Battle of Hastings.

programme.title: Wild China
programme.desc: Beneath billowing clouds, in China's far south west, rich jungles nestle below towering peaks. Jewel-coloured birds and ancient tribes share forested valleys where wild elephants still roam. These remote forests stretch into northern territories where normally deserts would be found. How do these forests exist? Perhaps the rugged landscape holds the key.

programme.title: Call My Bluff
programme.desc: Robert Robinson hosts the game of word definitions and deceptions. Team captains Frank Muir and Patrick Campbell are joined by guests Jenny Agutter, Tim Rice, Sinead Cusak and Nigel Dempster.

programme.title: Face the Music

programme.title: Horizon
programme.sub-title: Tim Peake Special: How to Be an Astronaut
programme.desc: In December 2015, Tim Peake became Britain's first astronaut on board the International Space Station. For two years, he had been filming a video diary for Horizon as he prepared to leave. From family life to the rigorous training, this is an intimate portrait and remarkable insight into the world of an astronaut.

programme.title: 8 Days: To the Moon and Back
programme.desc: The story of the Apollo 11 mission as told in the voices of the first men to set foot on the Moon. Using dramatic reconstruction, and declassified cockpit audio recorded by the astronauts themselves and film archive, this is the untold story of the first Moon landing.

programme.title: Great British Railway Journeys
programme.desc: From Wakefield, West Yorkshire, Michael visits the National Coal Mining Museum for England at Caphouse Colliery. He pauses to admire the tall spire of Wakefield Cathedral and its resident peregrine falcons before heading to the banks of the Calder.

programme.title: Wainwright's Walks
programme.desc: Julia Bradbury is in heart of the Lake District in the village of Grasmere for a climb up one of Alfred Wainwright's smallest but favourite fells. Helm Crag is defined by the collection of rock formations at its summit a feature that has lent it the nickname, the Lion and the Lamb. The rocks make for a summit scramble for Julia as she finds out why this was the only summit Wainwright himself never truly reached.

programme.title: Yes, Prime Minister
programme.desc: When a scandal breaks in the City, Jim Hacker and Sir Humphrey cannot agree on who should be the new governor of the Bank of England.

programme.title: Yes, Prime Minister
programme.desc: Jim Hacker meets a local councillor who has some radical ideas about local government. While the PM likes what he hears, Sir Humphrey is fearful it will weaken the Civil Service and must persuade him otherwise.

programme.title: Henry VIII's Enforcer: The Rise and Fall of Thomas Cromwell
programme.desc: Thomas Cromwell has a reputation as one of the most notorious thugs ever to hold power in England. Oxford University's Professor Diarmaid MacCulloch, reveals another side to Henry VIII's Chief Minister. Cromwell emerges as a pioneering and principled statesman. He ignited a religious and parliamentary revolution, which laid the foundations for the modern British state.

programme.title: Philip Larkin and the Third Woman
programme.desc: Former poet laureate Sir Andrew Motion discovers an unseen and unpublished poem by Philip Larkin when he returns to Hull to meet one of the poet's former lovers. Speaking for the first time about her relationship with Larkin, Betty Mackereth reveals the man behind the famous poems.

programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: For thousands of years, America's national mammal numbered in the tens of millions, sustaining the people of the Great Plains, whose cultures became spiritually intertwined with the animal.

programme.title: Wainwright's Walks
programme.desc: Julia Bradbury starts her walk in the quiet, mysterious valley of Mardale, where the local village was lost forever when the valley was flooded to create the Haweswater reservoir. The history continues as Julia climbs 2,500ft to the summit of High Street, the most well-trodden high ground in the Lakes. This was where Roman legions crossed the fells 2000 years ago, making, quite literally, a high street.

programme.title: Brian Cox's Adventures in Space and Time
programme.sub-title: Space: How Far Can We Go?
programme.desc: Brian explores the latest science and takes a new look at his old films and asks how far humanity can go in their exploration of the cosmos. Brian begins in Russia's cosmonaut training facility in the outskirts of Moscow.

programme.title: Tribe
programme.desc: Explorer Bruce Parry travels to the Amazon rainforest to live with the Matis, a tribe once devastated by western disease. They are determined to preserve their culture and they teach Bruce how to be a good hunter. He undergoes some gruelling tests including having painful tree sap dropped into his eyes and taking a powerful frog toxin to purge his system.

programme.title: Smiley's People
programme.desc: Vladimir has two proofs, but Smiley has only found one. It was an erotic photograph of Otto Leipzig, the General's lieutenant. Now aware that Vladimir has quarrelled with his postman Toby Esterhase, Smiley plans to visit old friends.

programme.title: Smiley's People
programme.desc: Smiley gets into trouble with his superiors whilst in Hamburg, but he leaves the city with valuable information. He now needs to get Maria Ostrakova to safety.

programme.desc: Andrew Marr argues that fantasy novels are filled with big ideas that allow us to see our own world in a surprising way, albeit through a twisted gothic filter.

programme.title: Olobobs
programme.desc: Mae'r Olobobs yn clywed cân snwff swynol - ond bob tro mae'r Olobobs yn ceisio closio at y Snwff Arbennig mae'n hedfan i ffwrdd. A all Bari Barfog eu helpu i ddysgu mwy am y creadur dirgel hwn?The Olobobs hear a beautiful snoof song but find it impossible to get near the special snoof - every time they approach it the snoof flies away. Can Twitchybeard help them learn more about this mysterious creature?

programme.title: Chwedlau Tinga Tinga

programme.title: Misho

programme.title: Guto Gwningen
programme.desc: Beth sy'n digwydd ym myd Guto Gwningen heddiw? What's happening in Guto Gwningen's world today?
